HO00007385.description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

HO00007386.title: Wicker
HO00007386.description: A fisherwoman lives on the fringes of a seaside village; she is unmarried, stinky, and constantly teased. One day, sick of her neighbors, she orders a wicker husband.

HO00007350.title: Wild Horse Nine
HO00007350.description: CIA agents Chris and Lee face a trust-testing mission from Santiago to Easter Island during 1973 Chile.

HO00007469.title: You Can See Everything
HO00007469.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move.

HO00007383.title: I Love Boosters
HO00007383.description: A group of shoplifters take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven by stealing her clothes and reselling them at a lower price, what they call "fashion-forward philanthropy.

HO00007368.title: The Social Reckoning
HO00007368.description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé

HO00007379.title: Wildwood
HO00007379.description: From the makers of Coraline, Wildwood is a sweeping, darkly magical adventure about Prue, a young girl who journeys into a hidden forest to rescue her younger brother.

HO00007419.title: Avengers: Doomsday
HO00007419.description: In “Avengers: Doomsday,” beloved heroes from three distinct universes will be set on a deadly collision course and face an existential threat unlike anything they’ve ever

HO00007375.title: Fatherland
HO00007375.description: FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika - actress, writer and rally driver.

HO00007462.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
HO00007462.description: War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant.

HO00007377.title: Klara and the Sun
HO00007377.description: Based on the bestselling novel from Nobel Prize-winner Kazuo Ishiguro and written and directed by Academy-Award® winner Taika Waititi (Jojo Rabbit), Klara and the Sun.

HO00007378.title: Possible Love
HO00007378.description: A story of two married couples — a laid-off worker and his spouse and a documentary filmmaker and her spouse — crossing paths to film a documentary...

HO00007372.title: Street Fighter
HO00007372.description: Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo) are thrown back into combat.

HO00007374.title: Clayface
HO00007374.description: Look fear in the face. DC Studios’ first-ever foray into the genre, “Clayface” is a horror thriller from director James Watkins, starring Tom Rhys Harries

HO00007349.title: Dune: Part Three
HO00007349.description: Dune: Part Three is set nearly two decades after Paul Atreides seized control of the Imperium. Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign.

HO00007353.title: Dune: Part Three - SPECIAL PREVIEW
HO00007353.description: Dune: Part Three is set nearly two decades after Paul Atreides seized control of the Imperium. Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign.

HO00007412.title: Fjord
HO00007412.description: A family faces mounting suspicion in a remote coastal town. Starring Academy Award nominees Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve.

HO00007431.title: Surprise Preview
HO00007431.description: Here's your chance to see a brand-new film before anyone else... take a leap of faith and join us for a surprise preview. No hints, no clues, just exclusive early access to conversation-starting cinema.

HO00007463.title: I Play Rocky
HO00007463.description: A struggling actor with a partially paralyzed face and a speech impediment writes a script that a big movie studio wants to buy.

HO00007486.title: Steps
HO00007486.description: Blamed for magical mischief at the Royal Ball, stepsister Lilith turns her sister into a frog. She must work with Cinderella and a troll to save the kingdom and prove vil

HO00007247.title: Shrek 5
HO00007247.description: Next summer, DreamWorks Animation invites audiences on a thrilling, magical new comedy adventure from one of the most beloved global animated franchises of all time

HO00007447.title: Film Club: Black Beyond: Blade
HO00007447.description: With his sword, sunglasses and leather jacket, Blade (Wesley Snipes) is instantly recognisable. The half-human, half-immortal hero leads this deliciously macabre pre-MCU Marvel movie, slaying bloodsuckers with considerable martial-arts skills.

HO00007442.title: Film Club: Black Beyond: Candyman
HO00007442.description: Folklore is embedded into Bernard Rose’s supernatural thriller, which takes place in and around the Chicago projects. The murderous Candyman (Tony Todd) terrorises its inhabitants, but his ancestral connection to slavery complicates his villainy.

HO00007448.title: Film Club: Black Beyond: Sorry To Bother You
HO00007448.description: Boots Riley’s bombshell of a debut centres on a down-on-his-luck telemarketer (LaKeith Stanfield), who quickly ascends the corporate ladder after adopting a white voice. Enlivened by eye-popping magical realism, it’s a searing technofascist critique.

HO00007446.title: Film Club: Black Beyond: Us
HO00007446.description: After rewiring our psyches with Get Out, Jordan Peele offers up another allegory about the Black American experience through his depiction of the Tethered, a substratum of imprisoned doppelgängers who symbolise the victims of mass incarceration.

HO00007451.title: NT Encore: The Motive and the Cue
HO00007451.description: The fierce and funny five-star play returns to the big screen. Sam Mendes directs Mark Gatiss in an Olivier Award-winning performance as John Gielgud.

HO00007126.title: RBO Cinema Season 2026-27: Così Fan Tutte
HO00007126.description: Spurred on by a bet, two young men hatch a plan to test the fidelity of their girlfriends. What follows is a slippery game of seduction and power.

HO00007382.title: Gentle Monster
HO00007382.description: After relocating with her family to the countryside, a renowned pianist uncovers a life-shattering truth that forces her to confront the complexities of love and trust.

HO00007430.title: Ken Russell's The Devils
HO00007430.description: An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award®-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession

HO00007316.title: Sense and Sensibility
HO00007316.description: From Focus Features and Working Title comes an irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love.

HO00007361.title: Digger
HO00007361.description: The most powerful man in the world embarks on a frantic mission to prove he is humanity's saviour before the disaster he’s unleashed destroys everything.

HO00007252.title: Queen at Sea
HO00007252.description: As dementia erodes a woman's ability to communicate her inner life, her husband and daughter struggle to act in her best interest, navigating love

HO00007432.title: Winter of the Crow
HO00007432.description: This gripping Soviet-era thriller features a mesmerising performance by Lesley Manville (Phantom Thread).  Based on a story by Nobel Prize-winning author Olga Tokarczuk.

HO00007182.title: Bitter Christmas
HO00007182.description: In this late-career gem, Almodóvar explores the gap between reality and fiction, inspiration and life.

HO00007471.title: Big Girls Don't Cry
HO00007471.description: Over one transformative summer in rural New Zealand in 2006, 14-year-old Sid discovers desire, identity, and the internet as she imitates the people she longs to be loved

HO00007307.title: De Gaulle: Part 2- Liberte
HO00007307.description: Charles De Gaulle's journey as a French army officer from 1940 to 1945, tracking his evolution toward a political career.

HO00007202.title: De Gaulle: Résistance
HO00007202.description: A powerful account of Charles de Gaulle's journey during World War II, from his rise as a military leader to his emergence in French politics between 1940-1945.

HO00007466.title: Josephine
HO00007466.description: After 8-year-old Josephine accidentally witnesses a crime in Golden Gate Park, she acts out in search of a way to regain control of her safety, while adults are helpless.

HO00007425.title: La Bola Negra
HO00007425.description: LA BOLA NEGRA tells the story of three men whose lives are intimately connected through desire, pain and inheritance, across three different eras – 1932, 1937 and 2017.

HO00007475.title: DocHouse: A Fox Under a Pink Moon
HO00007475.description:
At 16, Afghan artist Soraya is living in Iran with a violent husband, desperate to reach her mother in Austria and to live freely. She is a brilliant artist, channelling her fears into dark and beautiful sculptures and illustrations. 

This subtly textured self-portrait weaves chilling scenes of Soraya's escape attempts over five years, with news from Afghanistan and her visionary art, surreal animations and dancing. Many of her drawings, created along her escape route, feature recurring figures: a loyal fox who is her traveling companion, a pink moon that watches over her, and a clown who never laughs.

Filmmaker Mehrdad Oskouei worked entirely remotely, as Soraya filmed the footage herself using her phone. The result is a beautiful and profound portrait of survival, creativity and hope, which won Best Film at IDFA 2025.

HO00007487.title: DocHouse: American Doctor
HO00007487.description:
This timely film follows three doctors from very different backgrounds who travel to Gaza to volunteer in hospitals overwhelmed by war. 

Working amid bombardment, severe medical shortages and constant danger, the three doctors - Palestinian American emergency physician Thaer Ahmad, Jewish American orthopedic surgeon Mark Perlmutter and Zoroastrian trauma surgeon Feroze Sidhwa - bear witness to the devastating impact of the conflict on Gaza's hospitals in particular. 

When they return, they are compelled to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind, taking their battle from the front lines to the halls of Congress, and challenging prevailing media narrative from their first hand position.

Filmed on the ground in Gaza and back in the US, AMERICAN DOCTOR is a deeply human portrait of courage, compassion and moral responsibility.

HO00007439.title: DocHouse: Avedon
HO00007439.description:
From world leaders to pop culture icons, and international supermodels, Richard Avedon's influence helped create the blueprint for our image-driven world. His photographs didn't just reflect culture, they shaped it.

AVEDON traces the life and legacy of an artist who used photography to reinvent the world around him. Drawing on unprecedented access to his personal archives—never-before-seen stills, intimate behind-the-lens footage, and new interviews with his closest collaborators—the film explores how his singular eye both reflected and reshaped the visual language of the 20th century, and why even the most iconic image is only half the story.

HO00007408.title: DocHouse: Derek Vs Derek
HO00007408.description:
What do you do when your neighbour goes completely wild?
Award-winning director James Dawson’s new documentary is set in the rolling hills of Devon, telling the story of two neighbouring farmers who share the same name but take radically different approaches to land use. 

In equal parts hilarious and moving, the film shines a light on the vital debate surrounding the future of rural Britain, encouraging conversation around how farming and nature restoration might work together.

HO00007491.title: DocHouse: LDNDOCS 2026: The Great Experiment
HO00007491.description:
What happens when neighbors become strangers, when shared spaces become contested ground and when the very idea of a common future stops feeling possible? THE GREAT EXPERIMENT considers the results of what George Washington once called “our last great experiment” in democracy. Filmed in striking black and white across the US over four years, from 2017 to 2021, the film does not set out to adjudicate the political battles of its era but instead observes and engages the recent past with the critical distance of an archive.

Screening followed by a Q&A with Director Stephen Maing.

HO00007499.title: DocHouse: LDNDOCS2026: Illusions Of An Everlasting
HO00007499.description: Filmed over twenty-five years, The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer traces the lives of two inseparable cousins, Guillermina and Belinda, as they grow up in the vast Argentine Pampas. The film begins in 1999, when photographer-filmmaker Alessandra Sanguinetti invites her nine-year-old neighbors to share their dreams and fantasies, sparking a magical, deeply collaborative process that spans two decades. As Guillermina and Belinda leave childhood behind, their games take on the poignant weight of real-world desires and the realities of a male-centered rural life. The result is a portrait of female intimacy and friendship at once quiet and poetic, in which the fantastic and the mundane are intimately entwined. With the passage of time as its most palpable tension, the film becomes a bittersweet record of what changes and what remains in the inevitable arrival of adulthood.

HO00007421.title: DocHouse: LPFF 2026: Concrete Land
HO00007421.description:
An intimate story of three generations of a Palestinian Bedouin family in Jordan. Facing displacement and racism, their love and resilience are tested to the limit.

On the outskirts of Amman, the Najars are one of the last Afro-Palestinian-Bedouin families in the capital. Living in makeshift tents on agricultural land with their animals, they hold onto a way of life increasingly challenged by the rapidly changing city around them.

As pressure mounts from the authorities and their neighbours, the family is left isolated and unprotected, forcing them to confront what they must sacrifice to survive when their way of life is under threat. Through uncertainty and humour, the bonds between generations become their greatest source of hope and strength.

HO00007437.title: DocHouse: Making Marie Antoinette
HO00007437.description:
Eleanor Coppola turns her camera on her daughter, Sofia Coppola, as she shoots her 2006 historical drama, MARIE ANTOINETTE. 

Drawn from over 80 hours of behind-the-scenes footage shot on-set inside the Palace of Versailles, the documentary is a mother's view onto her daughter at work. Amongst the elaborate costumes and powdered wigs, Eleanor's insightful eye captures Sofia's strength, vulnerability and creativity as she directs the landmark film, aged 34.

HO00007410.title: DocHouse: Memorial / Liquidation
HO00007410.description:
In December 2021, Russia's Supreme Court ordered the liquidation of Memorial, the country's oldest human rights organisation, founded in 1987 to document and expose Stalinist terror. Ten months later, Memorial was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
Taisiya Krugovykh and Vasily Bogatov filmed the process from the inside. We see the court hearings and repression against the supporters of Memorial, the evacuation of the organisation's archive before its Moscow office is seized, and the trial of its co-chair Oleg Orlov on charges of "discrediting the Russian Armed Forces," which ends with his imprisonment.

Shot in the tradition of direct cinema, without commentary or voiceover, the film traces the dismantling of Russian civil society through the people who lived it. Both filmmakers have been in exile in France since 2022.

HO00007477.title: DocHouse: My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile
HO00007477.description:
When Russia shuts down all independent media, a group of young dissident journalists must flee Moscow so they can keep reporting and not go to prison.

In her riveting follow-up to last year’s awards-sweeping MY UNDESIRABLE FRIENDS - LAST AIR IN MOSCOW, Julia Loktev follows these courageous, sharply funny women (and a few men) as they fan out across a dozen countries, to Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, Vienna, Amsterdam, New York and beyond.

Over the course of four years, they continue to report the truth to Russians from exile, covering their country’s war crimes, even as they face death threats and are declared extremists and terrorists - as they find new meanings of family, friendship, love, and home far from the country to which they may never return.

HO00007415.title: DocHouse: NAZA
HO00007415.description: Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, NAZA reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

HO00007409.title: DocHouse: North Sea, Nature Untamed
HO00007409.description:
Peter van Rodijnen has travelled the world, capturing breathtaking footage of some of the most spectacular oceans, but what can he reveal about the cold, grey waters of his native North Sea?
Dive below the surface into an unexpected, fascinating ecosystem of marine wildlife. From the wild  waters around the Scottish islands to the shallow delta of the Low Countries and up along the dramatic coastline of the Norwegian fjords. NORTH SEA, NATURE UNTAMED is a cinematic adventure and a voyage of discovery showing the North Sea in all its glory.

HO00007435.title: DocHouse: One in a Million
HO00007435.description:
Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows one girl’s epic journey from Syria to Germany and back again. 

We first meet Israa at age 11, as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. As she settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilising pull of Szyrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. 

What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave.

HO00007438.title: DocHouse: Peter Asher: Everywhere Man
HO00007438.description:
Blending documentary and musical memoir, PETER ASHER: EVERYWHERE MAN tells the extraordinary life story of Peter Asher - pop star, producer, manager and confidant to legends from Paul McCartney to James Taylor, Linda Ronstadt, Carole King, and many more.

From his early years as a child actor in 1950s London to the Swinging Sixties, Asher emerges as a Zelig-life figure in the culture of the era; one half of the pop duo “Peter and Gordon”, recipients of four chart-topping hits penned by Paul McCartney; the first head of A&R at Apple Records; and co-owner of the Indica Gallery, the epicentre of London’s countercultural art scene.

Today, Peter Asher remains a vital creative force, still performing, producing and collaborating. EVERYWHERE MAN paints a vibrant portrait of Asher and his six decades at the heart of rock and roll.

HO00007440.title: DocHouse: Soul Patrol
HO00007440.description: From deep behind enemy lines, a hidden chapter of American military history is uncovered, prompting the question of whether reckoning with the past can bring peace to those who lived it. The Vietnam War’s first Black special operations team reunites to tell their story.

HO00007407.title: DocHouse: Steel on Film
HO00007407.description:
A journey through 50 years of Britain’s steel communities.
This event pairs Joe Cornick's impressionistic 16mm portrait of the final years of traditional steelmaking in Port Talbot, STEEL: THE BLOOD OF US (2026), with THE FACE OF CHANGE (1976),  Malcolm Hignett's documentation of the British Steel industry as it grappled with the seismic effects of recession and modernisation.
Made exactly 50 years apart, the two films offer contrasting perspectives on Britain's steel industry and the communities shaped by it.

HO00007406.title: DocHouse: The Eyes of Ghana
HO00007406.description:
A true love letter to cinema, THE EYES OF GHANA follows 93-year-old cameraman Chris Hesse, as he races against time to rescue a secret trove of film reels that uniquely captured the birth of African independence. 
Back in the 1950s and 1960s, Hesse was the personal cameraman to Ghana’s revolutionary leader Kwame Nkrumah. Always at Nkrumah's side and always filming, Hesse was witness to Africa’s tumultuous liberation movement. In 1966, Nkrumah was deposed in a coup and his rivals sought to destroy all the filmed records of his leadership, but Hesse found a way to preserve over 1000 reels.

Now in his 90s, Hesse is no less spirited and no less determined to pass on this celluloid legacy. He joins forces with filmmaker Anita Afonu to bring these barely seen reels to an audience in Accra, finally projecting a Ghanian perspective on their history. 

Filled with joy, verve and a dedicated focus on the importance of self-representation, THE EYES OF GHANA is a voyage through Ghanian cinema and a portrait of the country, from cinema’s inception through to the present day.

HO00007293.title: DocHouse: The Gardener, The Buddhist and the Spy
HO00007293.description:
A corporate spy in the pocket of the asbestos industry, or a whistleblower uncovering corruption? When Rob Moore invites two journalists to tell his story, the lines between intentions and consequences begin to blur.
For five years, former TV producer Rob poses as a filmmaker to gain the trust of anti-asbestos activists, whilst being paid to spy on them by the asbestos industry. When he is exposed as a cynical fraud, he claims to be a double agent, working alone to feed  false information to the international asbestos mafia.

In a bid to launder his reputation and regain credibility, Rob lets two journalists begin work on a podcast about him, but as they delve deeper into the shady case, inconsistencies and ethical dilemmas cast doubt on Rob's version of events.  One twist leads to another in a gripping film about the delicate balance between good, evil, influence and control.

HO00007488.title: DocHouse: To Hold a Mountain
HO00007488.description:
In the remote highlands of Montenegro, a shepherd and her teenage daughter hold on to a traditional rural lifestyle amid the growing pressures of the contemporary world.

Gara passes on her wealth of ancestral knowledge to Nada, as they herd animals, gather herbs, make cheese and live in symbiosis with the mountain and their community.

As Gara fights to defend their home from the threat of becoming a NATO military training ground, Nada must begin to think about her own future, as the pain of their family history is slowly revealed.

Winner of this year's Sundance World Documentary prize, TO HOLD A MOUNTAIN is a film rich in gently observed details, from the demands of pastoral labour to the love in domestic rituals.

HO00007436.title: DocHouse: We, The Hated
HO00007436.description:
WE, THE HATED turns a lens on the people behind one of the most polarising protest movements in recent history: Just Stop Oil. 

Director Rich Felgate, who is in a relationship with Just Stop Oil's founder, brings an insider closeness to the story, as the group go through actions, threats and repeated arrests. What emerges goes deeper than placards and road blocks: it's a portrait of individuals who have weighed up the personal consequences of action against the existential stakes of inaction.

With fossil fuels driving both the climate crisis and global conflict, and governments increasingly cracking down on dissent, the film raises urgent questions about protest, power and what democracy actually means in practice.

HO00007420.title: DocHouse: Women and the World Festival: Traces
HO00007420.description:
TRACES shines a light on Ukrainian women who, after surviving conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) and torture during Russia’s war, refuse to remain silent. 

Through the journey of Iryna Dovhan, a former captive turned activist, who documents testimonies of affected women on the de-occupied territories of Ukraine, the film weaves a collective portrait of trauma while opening space for hope. Iryna gathers other survivors into a circle of courage and care. Together, they transform their pain into a force for truth, justice, and mutual support. 

More than a document of war crimes, the film is a testament to resilience and the solidarity of women standing side by side.

HO00007489.title: DocHouse: You Can See Everything
HO00007489.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING.

HO00007445.title: Film Club: Black Beyond: In Fabric
HO00007445.description: Looking for a fresh start, a divorcée (Marianne Jean-Baptiste) buys a flattering, blood-red dress for a first date. However, it quickly becomes apparent that the garment has a life of its own, and goes on a killing spree in this giallo-inspired horror.

HO00007444.title: Film Club: Black Beyond: Neptune Frost
HO00007444.description: Neptune Frost, which premiered at Cannes, is a bold, afro-futuristic musical that follows a Rwandan miner (Bertrand Ninteretse) and intersex hacker (Cheryl Isheja and Elvis Ngabo) as they fall in love, and toggle between the real world and dream spaces.

HO00007460.title: Film Club: Raise The Red Lantern (4K Restoration)
HO00007460.description: A young woman becomes the fourth concubine of a wealthy man and soon realizes there's fierce competition for his attention and the associated privileges.

HO00007485.title: LDNDOCS 2026: American Doctor
HO00007485.description:
From Emmy® Award-winning filmmaker Poh Si Teng, American Doctor follows three American medics who travel to Gaza to volunteer in hospitals overwhelmed by war. Palestinian-American emergency physician Dr. Thaer Ahmad, Jewish American orthopaedic surgeon Dr. Mark Perlmutter, and Zoroastrian trauma surgeon Dr. Feroze Sidhwa come from very different backgrounds but are united by a shared commitment to save lives. Working amid bombardment, severe medical shortages, and constant danger, the doctors treat patients under extraordinary circumstances while witnessing the devastating impact of the conflict. They are compelled not only to care for the wounded but also to speak out about what they have seen.


Filmed on the ground as events unfold, this award-winning documentary follows their journey from besieged hospitals in Gaza to the halls of Congress in Washington, where they advocate on behalf of the patients and colleagues they left behind. A powerful and deeply human portrait of courage, compassion, and moral responsibility

Screening followed by a Q&A with Director Poh Si Teng, Dr. Thaer Ahmad, Dr. Mark Perlmutter, and Dr. Feroze Sidhwa.

HO00007490.title: LDNDOCS 2026: Bleeding Hearts
HO00007490.description:
Bleeding Hearts is an intimate documentary chronicling the whirlwind romance and musical collaboration between singer-songwriters Zella Day and Jesse Woods, who form the country duo Chaparelle. As they fall deeply in love, blend their distinct artistic styles, and pour their hearts into creating their debut album "Western Pleasure," the film captures the raw highs and lows of their journey; from passionate songwriting sessions and electrifying performances to financial struggles, creative tensions, touring exhaustion, and personal vulnerabilities. With producer Beau Bedford as their guide, Zella and Jesse navigate the fragility of blending love and art, confronting self-doubt, age differences, and industry pressures, ultimately emerging stronger as they sign a record deal, embark on sold-out tours, and get engaged, proving that true connection can fuel both heartbreak and triumph.

Screening followed by a Q&A with Director Andrew Morgan.

HO00007492.title: LDNDOCS 2026: Jean Michel-Basquiat
HO00007492.description:
Nearly four decades after his untimely death at age 27, Jean-Michel Basquiat is now one of history’s most celebrated artists. His work has been exhibited in every major art museum; it appears on everything from murals across the world to clothing and personal tattoos. But while his legacy is everywhere you look, parts of his life have been distilled into archetypes, elements of his upbringing omitted, and his story predominantly framed by the fine art marketplace. 

In  Jean Michel-Basquiat, Basquiat’s sisters, Lisane and Jeanine, lead an intimate and comprehensive portrait of their brother. Drawing on personal archives, never-before-seen works, and many voices of those who knew him best, this film illuminates the truth directly from the Basquiat family and allows Jean-Michel to finally guide his own story.

HO00007503.title: LDNDOCS 2026: Khosha: The New Land
HO00007503.description: Near the beautiful and mysterious Okavango Delta in the heart of Africa, eight members of the Khwe Bushman tribe – descendants of the oldest living human culture – embark on a long journey to find a new homeland. Forced to re-settle in villages, the Khwe are rapidly losing their culture. But this small group fights back, traveling to a new land called Khosha where they hope to find sufficient wildlife and medicinal plants to re-establish their hunting/gathering lifestyle. They take an old Khwe elder, who “feels” the land and crosses paths with the animals, and he issues a hopeful but haunting prophecy that soon comes true.

HO00007494.title: LDNDOCS 2026: Nuisance Bear
HO00007494.description:
Churchill, Manitoba sells itself as the “Polar Bear Capital of the World,” but what happens when the mascot becomes a problem? In their debut feature, Canadian filmmakers Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman track a polar bear through encounters with tourists, trucks, sirens, traps, wildlife officers, hunters, and relocation. The town profits from ursine spectacle, but Vanden and Weisman portray bears as neither scenery nor symbol. Instead, the bear becomes our protagonist, trapped in a system built to watch, sell, manage, and remove it.

Nuisance Bear overturns the nature documentary from the inside. Every chase, stare, and shutter click asks who is really intruding on whom. Moving between Churchill and the Inuit community of Arviat — with guidance and narration from late Inuit elder Mike Tunalaaq Gibbons — the film touches on issues of climate crisis, conservation, tourism, colonial settlement, and coexistence. Winner of the highly coveted Sundance Grand Jury Prize for Documentary, this is a formally daring work about spectacle, survival, and the violence hidden inside the word “nuisance”.

Screening followed by Q&A with Director Gabriela Osio Vanden

HO00007495.title: LDNDOCS 2026: Once Upon A Time In Harlem
HO00007495.description:
A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance. For four hours, this extraordinary group – many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years – reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape.

Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance. William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive.

Screening followed by Q&A with Producer Liani Greaves.

HO00007496.title: LDNDOCS 2026: Rehearsals For A Revolution
HO00007496.description:
Through five portraits of relatives and mentors, five expressions of resistance, Ahangarani sketches her life story. Drawing from personal archives, home videos, street protests footage, newspapers, and recorded voices, she retraces more than 40 years of Iran’s history. From the early days of 1979, until the war that began in 2026, she pieces together intimate and collective memories, forming the portrait of a country shaped by political repression and in constant hope for a revolution.

Screening followed by Q&A with Director Pegah Ahangarani.

HO00007493.title: LDNDOCS 2026: The Last First: Winter K2
HO00007493.description:
In “The Last First: Winter K2,” Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that takes an unflinching look at the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture. Focusing on a 2021 expedition, this documentary follows Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara, a party of mountaineers who set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and a Nepalese team no longer content to help Westerners achieve mountaineering glory. “The Last First: Winter K2” takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story — one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all under life-and-death circumstances.

Screening followed by a Q&A with Director Amir Bar-Lev

by diverse groups from Chicanx and Mexican identity, disability to queer
